title: Netflix's 'A Toxic Love Story' Unpacks the Bizarre True Crime Case of a US Marshal, His Wife, and a Frame Job
excerpt: The documentary, releasing today, tells the story of Michelle Hadley — arrested and jailed for 88 days on charges orchestrated by a couple who framed her using fake emails and a fabricated pregnancy.
body:
• A Toxic Love Story, a new Netflix true crime documentary, drops July 22 examining the case of US Marshal Ian Diaz and his wife Angela
  • Michelle Hadley, Ian's ex-girlfriend, was arrested and jailed for 88 days on fabricated charges of stalking and sending threatening emails
  • In 2017, Hadley was exonerated after investigators discovered Ian and Angela had framed her using fake email accounts, fabricated pregnancy tests, and orchestrated evidence
  • Directed by Alexandra Lacey and produced by Curious Films, the documentary features interviews with key figures and law enforcement

Netflix drops a new true crime documentary today that is already generating significant buzz. A Toxic Love Story unpacks the deeply strange case of Ian Diaz, a US Marshal in Anaheim, California, whose new wife Angela claimed they were being stalked by his ex-girlfriend — a claim that led to an arrest, 88 days in jail, and eventually, one of the most disturbing frame jobs in recent American criminal history.

The Setup

In May 2016, shortly after Ian and Angela married, the couple told friends and police they were receiving threatening emails from an anonymous account using the name "Lilithistruth." The messages had "biblical undertones," according to the documentary, and escalated to threatening Angela's allegedly unborn child. Some included images of "decapitated people" and "aborted fetuses."

All signs pointed to one person: Michelle Hadley, Ian's ex-girlfriend. In June 2016, Hadley, then 29, was arrested by Anaheim police. She spent 88 days in jail.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=9k9SYlMy9qs

The Unraveling

In 2017, Hadley was exonerated after investigators discovered the entire scheme had been manufactured. Ian and Angela Diaz had created the threatening email accounts themselves, fabricated pregnancy test results, and orchestrated the evidence trail to frame Hadley. The case was a sophisticated manipulation that exploited law enforcement's natural tendency to protect a fellow officer's family.

The documentary, directed by Alexandra Lacey and produced by Curious Films (the team behind Netflix's Lover, Stalker, Killer and The Man With 1,000 Kids), examines how the deception succeeded for as long as it did — and what it reveals about the intersection of law enforcement power, domestic manipulation, and the criminal justice system's vulnerability to fabricated evidence.

Why It Matters

Beyond the tabloid appeal, A Toxic Love Story raises questions about how easily digital evidence — emails, accounts, online activity — can be manufactured to destroy an innocent person's life. In an era where much of the evidence in criminal cases originates from electronic communications, the Diaz case is a cautionary tale about the gap between digital evidence and digital truth.

The documentary premieres globally on Netflix today and is available with subtitles in multiple languages, including Hindi.
